The PARTIALLY_KNOWN verdict survives. The lemma rests on three elementary steps: (i) the minimum is at most an average, which is Morwani's class-weighted margin g' >= g with tau a point mass on y - delta; (ii) the cosine expansion of the even part of a real function on Z_p, the same algebra as the variogram identity C(0) - C(h) = int (1 - cos) dF; (iii) Re(beta) <= |beta|. No fetched source states the per-offset amplitude-coverage bound for arbitrary networks. Sources checked: Morwani, Li et al. 2402.09469, He et al. 2602.16849, Mohamadi 2407.12332, 2511.23443, Gromov, Chughtai, 2608.04451, 2609.26679, and an OpenAlex title/abstract scan. All the checker's citations exist and say roughly what the checker says. The corrections below are needed.

1. Morwani locations.
- Theorem 7 is in Sec 4 and states the phase condition theta_u* + theta_v* = theta_w*.
- The Sec 4 proof outline uses uniform tau = 1/(p-1) and gives E[psi'] = 2/((p-1)p^2) sum u^v^w^(-j). Both confirmed.
- But eta_{u,v,w}(delta) := E[(u(a)+v(b))^2 w(a+b-delta)] and the phase-forcing step (cos(theta_u + theta_v - theta_w) = 1, Eqs. 7-8) are in Appendix F.1, not Sec 4. The eta citation in approach.tex should point to App. F.1.
- Lemma 5 is the single-neuron/combining lemma. The g' >= g inequality is in the Sec 3.2 text just before it.
- I checked the refinement claim by algebra: averaging the middle term over delta != 0 for the n = 2 power neuron reproduces Morwani App. F.1 Eq. (6) exactly.

2. McCracken bib fields. The paper is published: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 38 (NeurIPS 2025), pp. 49512-49573, DOI 10.52202/085713-1476 (resolved via Crossref CSL). It should be @inproceedings, not an arXiv @article. The current refs.bib entry (wrong title, 'Andrew McCracken and others') is confirmed wrong. Thm 4.7 (Sec 4.3) is confirmed. It models logits as h(k) = sum cos(2 pi f_l (k-i-j)/n) with random f_l and gives a probabilistic lower bound on separation, not an upper bound for arbitrary networks.

3. The checker understates the Kam et al. overlap (2609.17926, 15 Sep 2026).
- App. A.3.2 Eq. 15 is confirmed verbatim.
- Kam also pose the fixed-budget max-min allocation Delta*_S(B) = max_{||beta||_2 = B} min_s sum beta_k (1 - cos(omega_k s)). This is the paper's programme Gamma with an l2 budget on logit amplitudes.
- Their Proposition 5 proves uniform allocation optimal at full support (value Bp/sqrt(2(p-1))). The proof uses sum_{s != 0} (1 - cos) = p plus Cauchy-Schwarz, the same averaging step as approach.tex and cor:dense.
- They also report non-uniform numerical optima for restricted supports (+25% at K = 4, p = 47).
- Limits of their result: idealised aligned logits (Prop. 2 construction), budget on logit coefficients rather than weights, and the budget account explicitly disclaimed. So lem:phase itself is not in Kam, but the programme and cor:dense items must cite Kam Prop. 5 and Eqs. 15-16 as concurrent work.
- 'Heuristic loss proxy' is unfair: for their model the separation is exact and the loss bound is rigorous.

4. Missed related prior art for where eta_theta is introduced: Li et al. 2402.09469 (AISTATS 2025, already li2025nsum). Their Def. D.1 defines eta_{u1,u2,u3,w}(delta) for k inputs, and Lemma D.3 uses uniform class weighting. Cite it alongside Morwani.

5. Nanda Sec 4.2 is confirmed: logits approximated by sum alpha_k cos(w_k(a+b-c)), fitted by OLS, explaining 95% of variance.

6. No fetched page gave the spectral variogram / characteristic-function form of step (ii). Gneiting-Sasvari-Schlather 2001 was fetched, but its abstract lacks the formula. So no bib entry is recommended for it; it is elementary.

Recommended text:
- At eta: 'the network-level analogue of $\eta_{u,v,w}(\delta)$ of \citet[Appendix~F.1]{morwani2024feature} (see also \citealp[Definition~D.1]{li2025nsum})'.
- After lem:phase: '(the analogue of the phase condition in \citet[Theorem~7]{morwani2024feature}; averaging the bound uniformly over $\delta\neq0$ gives $\frac{p}{p-1}\sum_j\mathrm{Re}\,\beta_j$, which for their quadratic network is their uniformly class-weighted margin \citep[Appendix~F.1]{morwani2024feature}). For idealized phase-aligned cosine logits the right-hand side is the familiar logit separation \citep[Section~4.2]{nanda2023progress}, \citep[Theorem~4.7]{mccracken2025}. Concurrently, \citet[Appendix~A.3]{kam2026symmetry} bound the cross-entropy of such logits by the worst-offset separation and solve its $\ell_2$-budget allocation at full support.'

corrected_verdict: PARTIALLY_KNOWN. The lemma is an elementary adaptation of Morwani's class-weighted margin (Sec 3.2, tau set to a point mass on one offset) combined with the cosine expansion of eta (Morwani App. F.1 at the per-neuron level; Li et al. Def. D.1). Its right-hand side is the known separation for idealised aligned cosine logits (Nanda Sec 4.2, McCracken Thm 4.7, Kam Eq. 15). No source states it as an upper bound on the min-margin of an arbitrary network. Kam App. A.3.2 / Prop. 5 additionally overlaps the programme Gamma and cor:dense (l2 budget, full support); flag this to those items.

extra_citations.why: Corrects the checker's arXiv-only entry. Crossref metadata for DOI 10.52202/085713-1476 (via the OpenAlex record) gives NeurIPS 38, pp. 49512-49573. Sec 4.3 Thm 4.7 models logits as h(k) = sum cos(2 pi f_l (k-i-j)/n); its separation h(i+j) - h(k) is the equal-amplitude coverage.

App. A.3.2 Eq. 15 defines the worst-offset separation Delta_S(beta) = min_s sum beta_k (1 - cos(omega_k s)) for idealised aligned logits and bounds the loss by it. It also poses the l2-budget max-min allocation and proves uniform allocation optimal at full support (Prop. 5), which overlaps eq:programme and cor:dense. Concurrent (v1 15 Sep 2026, under review at NeurReps 2026).

Def. D.1 defines eta_{u1,u2,u3,w}(delta) = E[(u1+u2+u3)^3 w(a1+a2+a3-delta)], and Lemma D.3 uses uniform class weighting 1/(p-1). This is the k-input per-neuron precursor of eta_theta; cite it where eta_theta is introduced. Already in refs.bib; the arXiv abs comment reads 'AIStats 2025'.
